clue.text: Act of creating in common terms

definitions.text: Act of creating in common terms

parts.words: Act of creating in common terms
parts.note: to 'create' in everyday speech is to kick up a fuss; the phrase for making that fuss names a stage routine of singing and hoofing

explanation.definitionFit: A routine of singing and hoofing is a stage act, and making one about something colloquially means fussing or 'creating'.

clue.text: Domestic upheaval in taverns

indicators.note: an upheaval throws things into disorder, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some domestic disturbance has broken out in the local pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' reads as a household row, but here it is a noun: a household employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household employee such as a maid or butler.

clue.text: " So shines a good deed in a world" (Mer of Venice)

definitions.text: " So shines a good deed in a world" (Mer of Venice)

parts.words: So shines a good deed in a world
parts.note: Portia's line in The Merchant of Venice, with the missing adjective before 'world' to be supplied: a wicked, badly behaved world

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash before 'world' where the missing word goes; Portia says 'So shines a good deed in a naughty world'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective Shakespeare uses for the wicked world against which a small kindness shines like a candle.

clue.text: The sign of its final conjunction

definitions.text: The sign of its final conjunction

parts.words: The sign of its final conjunction
parts.note: the symbol & for the conjunction 'and' was once recited as the final item of the alphabet, 'and per se and'

explanation.walkthrough: Schoolchildren once ended the alphabet with '&', called 'and per se and', which slurred into the symbol's name; 'its' is the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for the conjunction 'and' and was once taught as the last character of the alphabet.

clue.text: One article in a non-alcoholic journal

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for non-alcoholic

parts.note: a dry area or event serves no alcohol
the Roman numeral I is one
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single piece written in a teetotal magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily personal record is a journal.

clue.text: 3 drops and includes a note of current measures'

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the note inside it
the word 'and' is let fall from the answer to 3 down

parts.note: the answer to 3 down, the symbol &
the word 'and' as written is the part removed
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that loses a word and gains a musical note to give units of current.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer of 3 down; 'drops and' removes AND from it, leaving AMPERS, and 'includes' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of electric current is named after André-Marie Ampère, so these are measures of current.

clue.text: Sea-rover said to have an ill-bred manner

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: coarse means ill-bred and an air is a manner

explanation.surface: A sailor of the high seas reputed to behave rudely.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate or privateer roving the Mediterranean, a sea-rover.

clue.text: Over on the village green do they leave Miss Bell 'standing?

definitions.text: Over on the village green do they leave Miss Bell 'standing?

parts.words: Over on the village green do they leave Miss Bell 'standing
parts.note: in village cricket an over is a set of balls; a ball skimming along the grass would mow down Daisy Bell, the girl of the song 'Daisy, Daisy', rather than leave her standing

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball bowled so low it rolls along the grass is said to cut the daisies; Miss Bell is Daisy Bell of the music-hall song, so the question's answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, deliveries that skim along the turf are named for mowing down the little white lawn flowers.

clue.text: Inflationary device showing pressure by the pound

definitions.text: Inflationary device showing pressure by the pound

parts.words: Inflationary device showing pressure by the pound
parts.note: the surface suggests economic inflation measured against sterling, but the device inflates tyres, its pressure gauged in pounds per square inch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflationary' and 'the pound' suggest economics; the device blows up tyres or balls, with pressure measured in pounds per square inch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand or foot pump blows up tyres and balls, inflating them with a measured pressure.

clue.text: Investment-in real trouble after a very quiet opening

indicators.note: the jumbled word comes after the opening piece

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

indicators.note: real in trouble is put into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An investment runs into real difficulties after a very quiet start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial but means what one is invested (clothed) in; the very quiet mark and A form the 'opening', with the jumbled word after.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment in its old sense is being clothed or robed, so it means clothing.

clue.text: Spills once seen in the streets at sundown

definitions.text: Spills once seen in the streets at sundown

parts.words: Spills once seen in the streets at sundown
parts.note: spills are paper or wood tapers for lighting a flame; the same name belonged to the men who went round lighting gas lamps in the streets at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spills' suggests accidents in the road; they are thin tapers used to light lamps, and the street gas-lamp tenders of old bore the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapers for kindling gas lamps, and the men who lit street lamps at dusk, share the name.

clue.text: Beauty butter-fingered in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a clumsy cook or washer-up who keeps breaking the crockery

explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a knockout a beauty, and the word also literally names someone who breaks plates.

clue.text: Extent of the law on shipping?

definitions.text: Extent of the law on shipping?

parts.words: Extent of the law on shipping
parts.note: a yard is an extent and an arm of the law reaches out; at sea, offenders were hanged from the spar at the masthead

explanation.walkthrough: A yard is a measure of extent and the law has a long arm; at sea, justice once meant hanging from a spar on the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a sailing ship's spar was where mutineers were hanged, the furthest reach of naval law.

clue.text: Short for smoking in Scotland

definitions.meaning: in Scots dialect the word means short or stubby
a short clay tobacco pipe, as named in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Scots uses the word for 'short', and so for a stubby clay tobacco pipe.

clue.text: Inherited from the rude ones in the Elegy?

definitions.text: Inherited from the rude ones in the Elegy?

parts.words: Inherited from the rude ones in the Elegy
parts.note: Gray's Elegy says 'The rude forefathers of the hamlet sleep', so what comes from those rustic forebears

explanation.walkthrough: Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' has 'The rude forefathers of the hamlet sleep'; 'rude' means rustic, not impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: What comes down from one's forefathers is inherited from forebears.

clue.text: Potential postman ?

parts.note: a post is a job or position, so one hoping to fill a post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Postman' suggests a letter carrier, but a post here is an appointment, and the potential post-holder is an applicant.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for an appointment is a would-be holder of the post.

clue.text: Camp character goes to study in Kent

parts.note: one who lives in a tent, as at a camp, is a tenter
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A theatrical type heads off to read in a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp character' suggests a flamboyant person, but it is a tent-dweller. TENTERDEN is a market town in Kent, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in the Weald of Kent, so it is a place found in that county.

clue.text: Everyone, for instance, in turn gets a flower

indicators.note: in turn means the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: everyone means all
EG is short for 'for example', for instance

explanation.surface: Each person takes a turn and is handed a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses ALL, EG and IN together, giving the plant called love-in-a-mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is a blue garden flower of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Bookmaker's issue

parts.note: a bookmaker suggests a betting shop, but here it is a publisher, whose issue is a printing of a book

explanation.walkthrough: A 'bookmaker' is usually a turf accountant (a betting-shop owner); here it is a publisher, and an issue is one printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's print run of a book or newspaper is an issue.

clue.text: Cast like the Stone that put the Stars to Flight

definitions.text: like the Stone that put the Stars to Flight
definitions.meaning: FitzGerald's Omar Khayyam: Morning 'Has ... the Stone that puts the Stars to Flight'

explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam opens with Morning having thrown a stone into the bowl of night to scatter the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast means thrown, and FitzGerald's Rubaiyat has the dawn hurling a stone into night.

clue.text: Proverbially heavy drinker consumes pop, uncommonly vain and affected

indicators.note: the drinker takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: one proverbially drinks like a fish

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of pop are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notorious boozer downs fizzy pop and turns out remarkably vain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy overconcerned with dress is vain and affected.

clue.text: Like Hamlet's "funeral bak'd meats" in June at Enfield?

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Hamlet's leftover funeral food turns up at a summer do in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'the funeral bak'd meats / Did coldly furnish forth the marriage tables': food left over from the funeral. ENFIELD is a north London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover funeral food served cold at the wedding had not been consumed.

clue.text: Single disruption by one kind of bomb causes such language !

indicators.note: disruption throws the word into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the hydrogen bomb

explanation.surface: One bomb's disruption makes someone swear!
explanation.walkthrough: 'such language' suggests swearing at a bomb's disruption; it is a nation's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the people of England is a language.

clue.text: Violently dislikes point being in the covers

indicators.note: the point is placed inside the covers

parts.note: hats cover the head
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Strongly objects to a sharp point in the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to dislike it intensely.

clue.text: Profoundly affected hearing of money advanced

indicators.note: hearing of means the next word is said aloud and a word that sounds the same is given

parts.note: deeply moved, made an impression on

explanation.surface: Someone was deeply moved on learning of a cash advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a loan or advance of funds, as to a public official for expenses.

clue.text: Man of note going it alone

definitions.text: Man of note going it alone

parts.words: Man of note going it alone
parts.note: a man of note sounds like a celebrity, but it is a musician playing a note alone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of note' suggests someone famous; here it is someone producing musical notes, performing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer playing an unaccompanied part in music goes it alone.

clue.text: A six at alternative ends — a real flyer !

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A big hit for six at either end of the ground: a real high flyer!
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six clears the boundary; here VI is the Roman six and OR, the word for an alternative, comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Step in then as required to make yourself a martyr

indicators.note: the letters are taken as required, rearranged to fit

explanation.surface: Advice to step in to become a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as required' rearranges STEP IN THEN AS into the first Christian martyr, stoned in Acts 7.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Christian martyr was stoned to death in Jerusalem, as told in Acts.
